summary: Build-time handling of is_in / t_is_in membership arguments. classify_members maps variadic Python arguments to a canonical member list purely by argument type (no backend or schema inspection) and raises typed errors for ambiguous, nested, native-expression or unsupported shapes; encode_membership turns the members into the (arguments, options) of the membership ScalarFunctionNode without coercion.
key_classes: MembershipArgumentError — base error (subclass of MountainashError) for invalid membership args
BareExpressionCollectionError — single bare expression passed as collection
NativeExprMemberError — backend-native expression used as member
key_functions: classify_members(args: tuple) -> list — type-driven canonicalisation (sets sorted by type rank then value)
encode_membership(...) — build (arguments, options) for the membership node; scalar literals use COLLECT_VALUES
is_backend_native_expression(x) — lazy check for polars/narwhals/ibis native expressions
lifecycle_notes: Introduced with the membership unification (spec section 4.1); no PR number recorded in git log for this path in this check
documentation_hooks: is_in / t_is_in argument semantics and error migration guidance
risks: encode must never route through ternary coercion (_coerce_if_needed) or members like str.lower() get booleanised
Set ordering depends on closed type-rank table (bool,int,float,str,bytes)

evidence.detail: classify_members decision tree, closed type-based rule
typed error hierarchy rooted at MountainashError
